definitions.explanation: Fish with dark red flesh, such as tuna and bonito: fast swimmers of the open sea whose muscles are rich in the red pigment myoglobin.

examples.japanese: ⟦マグロ→マグロ：11134_maguro⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{赤身魚|あかみざかな}だ。
{赤身魚|あかみざかな}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{鉄分|てつぶん}→鉄分：19444_tetsubun⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{多|おお}い→多い：01127_ooi⟧。
examples.english: Red-fleshed fish are rich in iron.

examples.japanese: カツオ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧ような{赤身魚|あかみざかな}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、⟦{広|ひろ}い→広い：00704_hiroi⟧⟦{海|うみ}→海：00556_umi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{速|はや}く→速い：00514_hayai⟧⟦{泳|およ}ぎ→泳ぐ：00545_oyogu⟧{続|つづ}ける⟦ため→ため：01145_tame⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{筋肉|きんにく}→筋肉：02646_kinniku⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{持|も}っている→持つ：00478_motsu⟧。
examples.english: Red-fleshed fish like bonito have muscles built for swimming fast across the open ocean.

notes:
RELATED WORDS:
- ⟦{白身魚|しろみざかな}→白身魚：21114_shiromizakana⟧: white-fleshed fish (cod, sea bream, flatfish)
- ⟦{青魚|あおざかな}→青魚：25871_aozakana⟧: blue-backed fish (mackerel, sardine, saury)
- ⟦{赤身|あかみ}→赤身：19617_akami⟧: lean red meat; the lean part of tuna

WATCH OUT:
Salmon has pink flesh but is classed as a ⟦{白身魚|しろみざかな}→白身魚：21114_shiromizakana⟧: its color comes from what it eats, not from its muscle.
